In this lesson you will learn about the Colpitts Oscillator.
INTRODUCTIONM
Colpitts oscillators change the DC operating voltage to a sine wave AC output.
The operation of a Colpitts oscillator is similar to a Hartley oscillator.
Only the components in the feedback circuit are different.i
Let's begin the lesson on COLPITTS OSCILLATOR OPERATION...................
LESSON MENU
COLPITTS OSCILLATOR
This is a typical Colpitts oscillator......................
DISCUSSION
The components in the feedback circuit produce an LC oscillator.
The split capacitors identify the oscillator to be a Colpitts.
To analyze circuit operation, divide the oscillator into its two circuits.
The amplifier circuit consists of Q1 and its associated components.
A common emitter amplifier is used. Notice that the transistor is an NPN.
R1 and R2 develop fixed bias on the base of Q1. R3 is the collector load resistor.
Q1output is routed through the feedback circuit to its input.
The feedback circuit consists of L1, C1 and C2.............
These components determine the frequency of oscillations.
When the LC tank is resonant, current flows through C1 and C2 in series.
Two capacitors are used to reduce the amount of feedback to the amplifier's input.
This prevents overdriving the amplifier.
C1 and C2 form a voltage divider. The input to the feedback circuit is developed across L1 and C2.
The output to Q1 is developed across L1 and C1.
The required phase shift is accomplished by the feedback circuit.
Checking for normal operation requires calculating the frequency of the resonant circuit.
Then measure the output frequency with an oscilloscope or frequency counter.

This is also a Colpitts oscillator. It uses two capacitors in the feedback circuit.
The operation is the same. Only the amplifier's biasing and the point where the output is taken from is different.
Fewer components are used and there is no temperature stabilization.
Taking the output of the oscillator from the output of the feedback circuit allows the amplifier to be biased class B or C.
Taking the output from the collector of an amplifier biased class B or C produces a distorted output waveform.
This circuit is also a Colpitts oscillator. It uses two capacitors.
However, the input to the feedback circuit is from the emitter to the center of C1 and C2.
In this oscillator, the input and output of the feedback circuit must be in phase since the base and emitter signals are in phase.
The in phase condition is accomplished by C1 being in series to the input and output of the amplifier.
The phase of a signal is the same through a series circuit.
The resonant frequency is still calculated the same.
Remember, a Colpitts oscillator uses two capacitors in the feedback circuit.

1. Colpitts oscillators are LC oscillators that use two capacitors in the feedback circuit.
2. The output of the amplifier is used as its input to produce oscillations.
3. The value of the components in the feedback circuit determine the frequency.
4. Colpitts oscillators can be made different. However, they operate the same.
